english_verification.read_scope: Read the full returned Markdown chunks for the two directly relevant English pages (Azjakuma and Horned Ogre); checked the local country history and name, the complete Y01 national-idea block and localization, representative mission/event text for the Chomora transition, and the current local country-name entries for similar countries Y89 and B54. Did not use the third unrelated search result.
english_verification.review_scope: Checked country identity and starting setup, idea names and scripted effects, and the representative event route that renames Y01 to Chomora and changes government and missions. Read both cited Wiki body chunks for historical context and source-boundary comparison. This is not a full mission-tree, event-chain, or community-source audit.
unresolved: The Azjakuma Wiki page says The Command demanded full subjugation in 1492; the Horned Ogre page says the Oni submitted as a slave state in 1492. The translated article records this difference without changing the Chinese-source research conclusion.

The Wiki describes the origins and chronology of spiritual siphoning as uncertain; the dates around 7325 BA and 7250 BA are presented as attributed historical accounts, not independently established dates.

The Dev Diary and player-discussion claims carried over from the Chinese article were not reopened during this bounded English-source check; their scope and experience claims are not independently verified here.

The stated total of 61 direct missions was preserved from the Chinese source but not independently recounted. Representative mission and event mechanics were checked, not the entire tree or every branch/reward.

rationale.complexity: Mission-phase changes, magic, subject management, and powerful enemies interact.
rationale.dark_story: The narrative explicitly depicts harm to souls and coercive rule.
rationale.difficulty: Managing several expansion fronts and magic demands substantial planning; not tested hands-on.
rationale.diplomacy: Subject management matters; conventional diplomacy is less central.
rationale.early_pressure: Powerful external threats, including The Command, create pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Devouring Path, mages, and the siphoning of spiritual energy are central.
rationale.narrative_density: A two-stage story runs from ancient fortress-temples to Chomora.
rationale.tall_play: Fortress-temple infrastructure matters, but the endgame pushes far outward.
rationale.trade_economy: Infrastructure and prolonged warfare require an economic base.
rationale.warfare: Conquest across Haless and conflict with powerful neighbors are the main axes.

identity.appearance: In 1444, a Horned Ogre theocracy following the Tagharoghi tradition; it can later be renamed Chomora under the same Tag.
identity.formation_scope: A dedicated event can rename the same Y01 Tag to Chomora (CHOMORA), change its government, and advance it to a new mission phase.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. Separate candidate sets and conditions are not treated as simultaneous; whether a new set is adopted on formation depends on the actual event/decision and the player's choice.

description.text: The Demon Hills are a twisted and treacherous landscape, full of dangers in the forms of beast, plant, and terrain. This is a land where only the strongest may thrive, and our enemies must face these obstacles should they desire to face us in battle.
description.text_en: The Demon Hills are a twisted and treacherous landscape, full of dangers in the forms of beast, plant, and terrain. This is a land where only the strongest may thrive, and our enemies must face these obstacles should they desire to face us in battle.

description.text: Many powerful forces have attempted to dislodge us from our Shirgrii, our castle monasteries. From the ancient human Rahenraj, to the fierce warlord Harimar, and even the mighty Jaher, all have failed. We have been here since they were but tribes with stone tools, and so we shall remain when all they own crumbles under the cruel hand of time.

description.text: Our land is an unimaginably ancient one - as far as the humans and tiger folk that rule around us are concerned, we have always been here. Throughout the millennia, we have gathered great and expansive archives of documents, treatises, and various other records. Our monks spend much of their time studying, maintaining, and updating these hallowed tomes.

description.text: Countless humans make the arduous trek through our lands to meet with us, either in an attempt to slay us in some venture to seem 'heroic' or to gather some of our antediluvian knowledge. Either way, all across Haless know of us, and countless stories about our people are spoken across the land.

description.text: We consigned ourselves to our Shirgrii long ago in repentance for our ancestor's betrayal of their True Giant masters. Repentance remains a valued virtue amongst our people, and we have countless elaborate and extensive rituals to cleanse oneself of their sins and regrets.
description.text_en: We consigned ourselves to our Shirgrii long ago in repentance for our ancestor's betrayal of their True Giant masters. Repentance remains a valued virtue amongst our people, and we have countless elaborate and extensive rituals to cleanse oneself of their sins and regrets.

description.text: Just as legendary as our wisdom and strength, we are widely known and feared for our incredible rage. While it may be quite difficult to truly infuriate an Oni, the result when one does is a reminder that, without our ascetic ways to keep us civilized, we are truly monsters.
description.text_en: Just as legendary as our wisdom and strength, we are widely known and feared for our incredible rage. While it may be quite difficult to truly infuriate an Oni, the result when one does is a reminder that, without our ascetic ways to keep us civilized, we are truly monsters.

description.text: For far too long we have let the world pass us by, locked up in our temples. For far too long we have allowed our enemies to come to us, instead of meeting them on the battlefield. For far too long, we have been denied our destiny by isolationists and cowards. Now, with threats on every side and upstarts at our doors, we shall remind them why one should not disturb a sleeping Oni.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who do not want brutal storylines, subject management, or pressure from The Command.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Build strength through mountain defense and infrastructure, then use magic, subjects, and conquest to advance a multi-stage imperial route.
player_overview.overview: Azjakuma is a Horned Ogre theocracy in the Demon Hills of Haless, anchored by fortress-temples, ancient knowledge, and magic that siphons spiritual energy. Develop the mountain strongholds and mage institutions first; later, the same Tag can be renamed Chomora and turn toward subjects, temple corruption, and hegemony over Haless. Its main storyline includes explicit soul siphoning and coercive rule, making it one of the setting's darkest country routes.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy sinister magic, hard mountain wars, and a long, dark imperial narrative.
signature_features: Ancient fortress-temples combine the roles of stronghold, library, and religious center.
A mission event renames Azjakuma to Chomora and changes its government while retaining the same Tag.
Mages, the Devouring Path, and spiritual siphoning drive the later expansion route.
player_overview.tagline: Defend the ancient fortress-temples, then turn the Devouring Path into a terrifying magical empire.

reasons: The fortress-temples and the Devouring Path create a distinctive setting.
The same-Tag, two-stage transformation supports a long campaign.
Magic and subject management are integrated into the expansion route.
warnings: The storyline depicts concrete acts of cruelty.
Powerful enemies and demanding mission requirements create substantial pressure.

positive_indicators: Protecting the clan's fortress-temples and preserving ancient knowledge.
values.rationale: The scripts and narrative text depict the siphoning of souls from captives, debtors, and defenders, as well as religious coercion. The low score is not based on ogre identity, ordinary warfare, or monarchy. The route is conditional, so the score describes the main tendency of the documented storyline.
red_flags: Using the souls of captives and debtors as a resource.
Draining defenders' lives and corrupting temples.
